vo.text: That color isn't random. It's a chemistry readout.
Urine's yellow tint comes from a pigment called urochrome.
Less water diluting it means a darker shade.
Guess which shade means you're well hydrated.
In 1994, researchers tested an eight-shade scale
Pale straw, shades one to three — that's well hydrated.
Ignore the neon yellow — that's riboflavin, not dehydration.
No app, no wearable. Just look before you flush.

pointer slides back to bands 1-3; WELL HYDRATED label + r=0.80 stat chip
separate neon-yellow riboflavin swatch, OFF the scale; pointer unchanged
dissolve back into hook composition, grow zoom, no CTA

urine_color.source: Armstrong LE et al., International Journal of Sport Nutrition, 1994
urine_color.confounder: riboflavin (vitamin B2) fluoresces bright/neon yellow independent of hydration
